state.location: Sun–Earth L2 (1.5 million km from Earth)

spacecraft.name: ESV Calliope
spacecraft.notes: Small short-range research vessel. Cannot yet leave the Earth–Moon–L2 neighbourhood.

instruments.name: Meridian 2.4 m Optical Telescope
instruments.limitations: Cannot see through dense dust, so the Galactic Centre and distant compact objects are out of reach. Exoplanets can only be studied through their host stars at this stage.
instruments.description: A segmented-mirror optical telescope on a deployable boom, tuned for stellar photometry and imaging of nearby objects.

instruments.name: Halcyon 15 m Radio Dish
instruments.limitations: Poor angular resolution. Only nearby stars and bright radio sources are practical targets. Cannot reach very distant quasars.
instruments.description: A steerable dish with cryogenically cooled receivers. Radio waves pass through interstellar dust, which makes it the first instrument able to listen to the Galactic Centre.

discoveries.title: Characterisation: Proxima Centauri
discoveries.summary: 12 h optical observation of Proxima Centauri analysed (data quality 84%). Results are consistent with the catalogue characterisation of this red dwarf star. Catalogue values: see Universe Explorer.
